summary: Long-tail latency spikes and intermittent request timeouts when using JSON_OUTPUT mode for large structured replies
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LuminaDocs reports a large increase in tail latency and occasional timeouts when using the API's JSON_OUTPUT mode to generate large structured documents (40-200KB). The failures started after the customer moved from a simple text template to the new structured schema validation and streaming-json post-processor.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for one key API route are hitting >5s tail latency, and ~1.8% are returning 504s.
- Customer-facing feature (document generation pipeline) slowed; customers reported degraded UX and timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for LuminaDocs in prod us-east.
- Request pattern: streaming responses with JSON_OUTPUT, large arrays nested under "pages" and per-item metadata.
- Model variants observed: redwood-open-7b-v2 and community-13b-q4_k with automatic fallback enabled.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) POST /v1/generate with mode=JSON_OUTPUT and schema v2 (embedded validator).
2) Provide prompt that yields ~150-350 tokens per array item and 20-50 items.
3) Enable streaming and client expects newline-delimited chunks that assemble into final JSON object.

Observed behavior:
- Normal throughput for first N-1 chunks, then a pronounced CPU spike on json-decoder workers for the final tokens.
- Streaming connection remains open but no bytes transmitted for ~2-6s before final chunk; sometimes results in HTTP 504.
- Logs show repeated "schema-enforcer: backpressure" traces and decoder retries on final tokenization step.

Expected behavior:
- Smooth streaming with small finalization delay for closing JSON. No long-tail spikes or timeouts.

Preliminary hypothesis:
1) The structured JSON post-processor (schema-enforcer + strict validator) runs a synchronous validation pass that becomes O(n^2) with many nested items, causing final token decode to block and oversubscribe event loop.
2) The streaming assembler waits for the validator to fully parse the buffered chunks before emitting final bytes; when validation stalls, network flush is delayed.
3) Fallback routing may trigger additional model warmups mid-stream (rare) which exacerbates the spike.

Relevant logs and artifacts:
- Customer-provided request ID examples: req_us-1234-20260309a, req_us-1234-20260311b
- Metrics snapshots: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latency?range=2026-03-09..2026-03-11&customer=LuminaDocs
- Heap/CPU flamegraphs attached by the customer (S3 link): s3://lumina-artifacts/json-decode-spike-20260311.tar.gz

Notes on customer urgency:
- LuminaDocs is a dedicated customer with high-volume daily runs. They requested an update within 48 hours and asked for a mitigation to reduce timeouts.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:40 - Ethan: Replayed sample requests in staging. Reproduced long-tail delay when schema size > ~80KB. CPU on json-decoder process climbs to 220% on 4vCPU container.

2026-03-10 12:15 - Eng on-call (Anika R.) : Confirmed synchronous validator runs during end-of-stream finalize(). Observed lock on decoder's parse mutex for ~2.2s before final bytes flush. Opened internal ticket INT-341 for potential async validator work.

2026-03-11 08:05 - SRE (Tomas): Collected pprof; stack traces show heavy GC and repeated attempt to allocate large transient objects inside schema-enforcer. Memory churn correlates with number of array items.

2026-03-11 14:30 - Ethan: Tested fast-path by disabling strict validation flag on post-processor; tail latency dropped from 2.3s median to 120ms for final chunk. Throughput recovered and no 504s observed in test window.

2026-03-12 10:00 - Performance team: Kernel selection not implicated (same behavior across GPU/CPU-backed instances). Root cause appears computational complexity in streaming validation/assembly step.
workaround: Short-term mitigations active for LuminaDocs: 1) Disable strict server-side schema validation for large responses (flag: json_validators.strict=false) — customer accepted for now. 2) If strict validation is required, recommend client-side validation: request raw TEXT stream + client performs schema check. 3) Route heavy requests to a model variant with lower per-token overhead (community-13b-q4_k showed similar but slightly better behaviour).
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-11: disabled strict validator for the affected customer route and increased request timeout to 12s for a rolling 24h window. Monitoring configured to alert if >1% servers hit >3s finalization delay. Engineering next steps: implement async validation pipeline that validates chunks incrementally and emit final bytes without blocking event loop; target PR and benchmark by 2026-03-20. Linked internal task INT-341 created to track implementation details.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:00 - Sophie Patel (Customer Success): Logged initial ticket after call with LuminaDocs. Customer provided example payloads and consented to temporary validation disable. Asked for plan within 48h.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Ethan Morales (Support): Acknowledged. Reproducing locally and assigned to eng on-call. Will report findings by EOD.

2026-03-11 15:20 - LuminaDocs (Kevin M.): Noted improvement after we disabled strict validation. Small number of outputs still appear with slow tail (~1/1000). Customer requests permanent fix timeline.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Anika R. (Eng on-call): Added INT-341 and initial design notes. Async incremental validator sketch posted to PR thread: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3189
